answer.summary: Protected deep-work time is a deliberately reserved, interruption-free block of roughly three to four hours for creative and strategic work, rather than meetings. Megan’s leadership team synchronized calendars to create shared stretches twice a week, while leaving calendar flexibility for urgent collaborative work and extra manager-report discussions.

sections.heading: What the time is for
sections.content: It is time set aside and protected so people can focus on creative work and get into a flow state; it is not time for routine meetings or casual interruptions. Megan says scattered meetings with only 30-minute gaps do not provide the three to four hours needed to get into that work.

sections.heading: How her team made it work
sections.content: Megan and her leadership team synchronized their calendars to create long shared blocks twice a week—one afternoon and one morning. This reduced meeting availability, but also left shared time to handle unexpected work together. She separately kept calendar flexibility for reports who needed more time on an issue, such as a difficult strategy problem.
